d: a large box-like structure (the vessel built by Noah)
a larger ocean-going vessel used for transporting cargo and people
an identifying emblem, possibly a carved figurehead at the prow of a ship
a large plank at the stern of a ship used to direct its course
(a diminutive form of {L:πλοῖον<SDBG:πλοῖον:000000>} ‘boat, ship,’ {D:6.41}, but in some contexts it is possible that the diminutive aspect of πλοιάριον is not relevant) small fishing boat
any kind of boat, from small fishing boats as on Lake Galilee to large seagoing vessels
the back part of a boat
a heavy object attached to a boat by a rope or chain and dropped to the bottom of a body of water in order to prevent or restrict the movement of the boat
a small boat which was normally kept aboard a larger ship and used by sailors in placing anchors, repairing the ship, or saving lives in the case of storms
a cloth attached above a boat in such a way as to catch the wind and thus propel the boat through the water
